title: How Milburn won over Labour on tackling rising youth unemployment
summary_full: Labour grandee seems to have assuaged MPs’ nerves on need for welfare reform to tackle youth unemployment crisisIn a boxing gym in Peterborough almost a year ago, Alan Milburn, freshly appointed to run a government review into the nearly one million young people out of work and education, said he would be “unafraid to shine a light on uncomfortable truths”.The Labour grandee, who had held three cabinet jobs under Tony Blair, warned there was a “downward escalator” taking young people into a “world of benefits” and vowed to provide radical solutions. Many Labour MPs bristled. Continue reading...
